idiom_name: generic phantom state parameters on a wrapper class + extension-method transitions
implementation_notes: C# generics can carry phantom state parameters: sealed marker classes (Unset, Set) parameterize the wrapper type, each state has its own extension methods, and a transition returns the next instantiation while the terminal operation is declared only for the settled one. The classic structure's linearity half is unavailable - assignments copy references, so a stale state value stays usable and the guarantee covers which operations exist, not that the old state is gone. Source generators automate the builder case (TypedStateBuilder), and for presence-only requirements C# 11's required members are the lighter, compiler-enforced alternative.
pitfalls: Reference semantics: after a transition both the old and the new variable are alive, so keep the state value in one place or make the wrapper a readonly struct and discard the old variable.
C# has no higher-kinded types and a partial class cannot declare different constraints per part, so per-state members must be extension methods over distinct instantiations.
If the marker interfaces are public, inference can widen a value to the interface and erase the state; keep markers sealed and internal.
